chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, all from Ibn Mahboub, from Khalid ibn Jarir, from Abu Al-Rabie Al-Shami, who said:

Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) was asked about wine, so he said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent me as a mercy to the worlds, and to obliterate the musical instruments, and the pipes, and the affairs of the Pre-Islamic period, and the idols.'

And he (peace be upon him) said: 'My Lord swore that no servant of Mine will drink wine in the world except that I shall give him to drink of its equivalent from the scalding water on the Day of Resurrection, punished or forgiven; and no servant of Mine will give it to a young child or a slave except that I shall give him to drink of its equivalent from the scalding water on the Day of Resurrection, punished afterwards or forgiven.'

key_terms.الْحَمِيم: Scalding water (a specific drink in Hell)

ai.seo_question: What is the specific punishment for drinking wine mentioned in this hadith from Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), who attributes the prohibition of wine to the Prophet Muhammad (PBUH), framing it as part of eradicating Jahiliyyah customs like music and idols. The hadith highlights a specific divine vow (qasam Allah) where the drinker is quenched with an equivalent measure of scalding water (hamim) on the Day of Judgment, illustrating the principle of proportional retribution (muqabalah) in divine justice.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, and a number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Khalid Bin Jareer, from Abu Al Rabie Al Shamy who said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> was asked about the wine, so he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Mighty and Majestic Sent me<sup>saww</sup> as a Mercy to the worlds, and for the obliteration (destruction) of the musical instruments, and the affairs of the Pre-Islamic period, and the idols’.

And he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘My<sup>saww</sup> Lord<sup>azwj</sup> Vowed: “A servant of Mine<sup>azwj</sup> will not drink wine in the world except that I<sup>saww</sup> shall Quench him<sup>as</sup> similar to whatever he has drunk from the scalding water on the Day of Judgement as a Punishment, regardless of there being Forgiveness for him; nor would any servant of Mine<sup>azwj</sup> drink it, be he a young child or an owned slave, except that I<sup>azwj</sup> would Quench him from the scalding water on the Day of Judgement, as a Punishment afterwards, regardless of there being Forgiveness for him”.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father and Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and a number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad all from ibn Mahbub from Khalid ibn Jarir from abu al-Rabi’ al-Shamiy who has said the following:

“Once abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, was asked about wine. Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, sent me as mercy for the worlds. (Allah sent me) to eradicate playing tools, musical pipes and matters of the age of darkness, ignorance and idols.’

He (the Messenger of Allah) has said, ‘My Lord swears and says, “If any of My servants in the world drinks wine I will make him drink al-Hamim (boiling water of hell, that roasts the face when drinking) on the Day of Judgment, regardless of whether he will be made to suffer or will be forgiven. If anyone makes a child to drink wine or a slave, I will make him drink the same amount of al-Hamim, regardless of whether he will be made to suffer or will be forgiven.’”
